slides.title: An Infectious Disease Spread Simulation Based on Large Language Model Decision Making
slides.highlight: This research develops a spatially grounded agent-based simulation using LLMs to model individual decision-making and behavioral dynamics during disease outbreaks, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: An agent-based simulation using LLMs to model demographically and spatially grounded infectious disease reporting behaviors.
card.key_idea: Replaces rule-based/logistic regression decisions with LLM-generated responses based on census-derived demographic profiles and situational contexts, utilizing a pre-generated decision bank for scalability.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in San Francisco and Atlanta using four open-source LLMs; compared against logistic regression and UAS vaccine intent data for directional validity.
card.limitation: LLM outputs show sensitivity to prompt wording and contextual richness, which may introduce variability in policy-oriented applications.

slides.title: Revising Context, Shifting Simulated Stance: Auditing LLM-Based Stance Simulation in Online Discussions
slides.highlight: This research evaluates the context sensitivity of LLM-based simulations of user stances in online discussions, which is relevant to MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: This paper introduces a counterfactual context revision framework to audit LLM-based social media stance simulation.
card.key_idea: The authors apply controlled text-only and multimodal (meme-based) revisions to conversational contexts to measure how LLM-simulated user stances shift in response to context changes.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using average directional stance shift and stance transition rate across different polarization-preference mechanisms; results show robust stance transitions.

slides.highlight: The launch of a world model lab to scale humanoid intelligence is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

slides.title: Benchmarking Counterfactual Prediction in Epidemic Time Series with Time-Varying Interventions
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING COUNTERFACTUAL PREDICTION IN EPIDEMIC TIME SERIES
slides.highlight: This work introduces a large-scale benchmark for counterfactual prediction in epidemic time series using a calibrated agent-based model, which is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Introduces EpiCF-Bench, a large-scale benchmark for counterfactual prediction in epidemic time series using calibrated agent-based models.
card.key_idea: Uses a differentiable agent-based model (ABM) grounded in real-world demographic and mobility data to simulate factual and counterfactual COVID-19 trajectories across 158 U.S. counties.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using 158 U.S. counties; ABM calibration achieved a mean NRMSE of 0.1887 against CDC case data. Baselines include KDE, Transformer, CVAE, and CDiffusion.
card.limitation: The ABM's structural rigidity can cause optimization to fail for highly irregular multi-wave behaviors, requiring manual filtering of unsuccessful calibrations.

slides.title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios
slides.highlight: Ouvia provides a framework for measuring the usability of speech translation in real-world one-to-one communication, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: Ouvia is a user-centered framework measuring speech translation usability through real-world, situated communication scenarios.
card.key_idea: A multi-phase protocol involving senders, receivers, and bilingual validators to assess if translations successfully convey key information across diverse demographic groups and high/low-stakes contexts.
card.evaluation: 1,738 interactions across four ST systems (English-to-Portuguese). Evaluated via 5-point Likert scales, QA scores, and automatic metrics (e.g., COMET, XCOMET). Results show significant demographic usability gaps.
card.limitation: Limited to one language pair, uses scripted/clean speech instead of spontaneous conversation, and relies on crowdworker validators.

slides.title: Regret Minimization with Adaptive Opponents in Repeated Games
slides.tldr: NEW REGRET METRIC FOR ADAPTIVE OPPONENTS IN REPEATED GAMES
slides.highlight: Introduces Repeated Policy Regret (RP-Regret) to account for counterfactual reasoning and adaptive opponents, supporting the development of agent models for harmonious hybrid human-AI societies in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Introduces Repeated Policy Regret (RP-Regret) to handle adaptive opponents in repeated games, promoting cooperative equilibria.
card.key_idea: A game-theoretic metric accounting for counterfactual reasoning and opponent adaptivity, minimized via non-convex oracles, linearized surrogates (LRP-Regret), or Markov game reformulations.
card.evaluation: Theoretically analyzed via necessary conditions for sublinear regret; experimentally demonstrated to find higher-utility cooperative solutions in games like Stag-Hunt.
card.limitation: Direct minimization is non-convex; sublinear regret requires specific constraints on comparator variation and exponential decay memory (imperfect recall).

slides.title: LLM Explainability with Counterfactual Chains and Causal Graphs
slides.highlight: This research proposes a method to model LLM inference using causal graphs and counterfactual chains, supporting MIMIC's focus on neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: A framework that explains LLM classification by constructing causal graphs over human-interpretable concepts.
card.key_idea: A four-phase pipeline using LLMs for concept discovery, an MCMC-inspired counterfactual augmentation to densify the concept space, and $\sigma$-CG for stable causal graph discovery.
card.evaluation: Tested on three LLMs across disease diagnosis, sentiment analysis, and LLM-as-a-judge tasks using predictive fidelity and structural stability metrics.
card.limitation: Relies on the target LLM for self-annotation and counterfactual generation, which may introduce unfaithful reasoning or propagation errors.

slides.title: Causal Longitudinal Prior-Fitted Networks for Counterfactual Outcome Prediction
slides.tldr: IN-CONTEXT PREDICTOR FOR LONGITUDINAL CAUSAL PREDICTION
slides.highlight: CausalLongPFN uses synthetic causal pretraining to predict counterfactual outcomes and future trajectories, supporting the simulation of complex agent dynamics relevant to MIMIC.

card.one_liner: CausalLongPFN is a frozen, in-context predictor for longitudinal counterfactual outcomes pretrained on synthetic causal models.
card.key_idea: A dual-encoder transformer pretrained on a broad prior of temporal structural causal models, using support trajectories for zero-shot, in-context potential-outcome prediction via autoregressive rollout.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on cancer, HIV, warfarin, and MIMIC-III benchmarks against domain-trained baselines using normalized RMSE; competitive on one-step and best on factual MIMIC-III prediction.
card.limitation: Performance depends on the synthetic prior's coverage and requires standard longitudinal causal assumptions (e.g., sequential exchangeability) to be valid.
